name: ufsmodules
description:
EVERY MODULE /etc/modload.conf NAMES IS UP ON A UFS ROOT, which is the half of Phase 2's gate that says 'no ProDOS module loaded at all'.  The kernel announces `mod: <name> loaded' from Mod_RegisterStreamed for every module however it arrived, so these five needles are the same evidence whether the KERNEL read modload.conf or userland ran modload(8) -- which is the point, because that is exactly the transition this test is here to survive.  THE NEEDLES CANNOT COME FROM THE COMMAND: they are kernel announces printed during boot, before anything is typed, and the manifest's command is a bare prompt-reacher.  WHAT IT DISCRIMINATES, measured 2026-09-03: on disk/fgxroot.fs only vfs, ufs and ufsdir appear -- they are segments of /fgxunix and delivered by the boot program -- and all five of these are ABSENT, because Mod_LoadConf runs in the kernel (main.s:692) and reads through Fs_ReadN, which answers EBADF for a root descriptor.  The consequence is visible two lines further down the same boot log as `dhclient: no network interface' and `inetd: telnet/tcp: socket: Function not implemented'.  On disk/fgx.po the same five are present, so the assertion is not merely absent-on-both.  apple/fgx#309 made SYS_MODLOAD able to install them from userland; this test is what says whether anything does.

THE MODULE LINE IS `module: <name> loaded' SINCE 2026-09-06, and it is the KERNEL's -- printed only after mod_init returned success.  modload(8) used to print a second line about the same event, in the conf file's spelling (SERIAL) rather than the module's own (serial); it is silent on success now, as every other tool on this volume is.
